_comment: Tier-2 for NGSolve heat#2, a catalog-drift correction: the prior claim that GridFunction storage grows 'only after gfu.Update()' was wrong. Measured on 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh=0.5, H1(order=1): before Refine fes.ndof and len(gfu.vec) are both 8; after mesh.Refine() and WITHOUT any Update call, len(gfu.vec) already reads 21 -- and it is read FIRST so the ndof access is not what triggers it. FINDING: the claim's 'does not carry a prolongation of the old solution' is FALSE. Measured, the old DOF values are preserved entry-for-entry and the new DOFs are interpolated, not zero. The advice to re-solve is still right for a different reason -- the prolongated function is the coarse function re-expressed, so the representation error is bit-for-bit unchanged by the refine and only a re-Set improves it. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented fix where a user would apply it -- gfu.Set(curved) immediately after mesh.Refine(), so the stale prolongated coarse function never reaches the measurements. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 10 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'old_dof_values_preserved=True' (the re-Set overwrites the coarse DOF values) and 'refine_alone_buys_no_accuracy=True' (the error drops 4.40e-2 -> 1.08e-2 instead of staying bit-for-bit equal), and the forbidden string 'FAIL:' appears, so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
